causal_chain: A separate exclusion prototype built from cross-slot disagreement can encode items that are near some historical evidence but inconsistent with the user's dominant co-occurring intents.
A small set of user-specific intent slots built from attention over historical item embeddings can preserve distinct preference modes during pairwise training.

At scoring time, routing a candidate through the best-matching intent slot while subtracting gated exclusion alignment should raise scores for coherent niche positives and lower scores for misleading broadly similar items.
This sharper intent-selection-plus-repulsion mechanism should improve full-sort NDCG@10 relative to a matched single-vector pairwise control.
Users in ML-1M often express multiple stable tastes that a single embedding compresses into an average preference vector.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from using interaction-history aggregation at inference, producing a stronger user representation through extra capacity, rather than from the specific combination of multi-intent routing and exclusion subtraction.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with a mechanism-off mean-history dot-product control using the same item embeddings and pairwise optimizer, the proposed model should show larger improvement for users with longer and more diverse histories than for short-history users.

If multi-intent routing is causal, the winning intent slot for a user's held-out positives should vary meaningfully across candidates for mixed-taste users, whereas the mechanism-off control has no candidate-specific user-state selection.

If the exclusion channel is causal, score reductions should concentrate on popular or cross-genre distractor items that align with one intent slot but conflict with the routed slot, not uniformly across all negatives.
expected_evidence: Ablating exclusion while keeping multi-intent slots should reduce the benefit specifically on users whose histories span weakly compatible item clusters.
Higher full-sort NDCG@10 than the executable mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Positive items for mixed-history users receive higher routed-slot affinity than mean-history affinity, while common distractors receive stronger exclusion penalties.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the matched mechanism-off control matches or exceeds NDCG@10, or if routed-slot assignments collapse to a single slot for most users with no measurable exclusion effect on distractor scores, the hypothesis is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This changes the core representation from one user embedding to a candidate-routed set of intent slots plus an explicit exclusion prototype, changes the interaction structure from static bilinear matching to slot selection with subtractive gating, and introduces a custom executable capability for per-user history-conditioned scoring absent from the active profile catalog.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that represents each user as a small mixture of intent slots derived from the user's historical items and scores each candidate through routed attraction minus a learned exclusion prototype will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-vector collaborative filtering because it preserves multi-interest structure while explicitly suppressing near-miss distractors.
implementation_requirements: Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with user embeddings, item embeddings, K global intent query vectors, and an exclusion projection module in PyTorch.

Implement an executable mechanism-off sibling in the same file that replaces routed multi-slot scoring and exclusion subtraction with a single mean-history user representation dot product under the same optimizer and data flow.
Precompute each user's interacted item ids from the train matrix only and build user intent slots by attention pooling over that user's historical item embeddings during forward passes.
Provide full-sort prediction by batching users, recomputing or caching train-only intent slots, and scoring against all candidate item embeddings without reading held-out interactions.

Score a user-item pair by computing candidate-conditioned routing weights over the K intent slots, taking the routed attraction score, subtracting a sigmoid-gated exclusion alignment term, and training with BPR loss.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same train matrix, item embedding dimensionality, optimizer family, pairwise loss, regularization budget style, and evaluation pipeline as the proposed model, differing only by collapsing the representation to a single mean-history vector and removing exclusion gating.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace static user scoring with a history-conditioned multi-intent slot constructor plus candidate-specific routing and subtractive exclusion gating.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is an executable single-channel history-aggregated matrix-factorization control: compute one user vector as the attention-free mean of that user's train-history item embeddings, score candidates by dot product with item embeddings, train with the same BPR objective and embedding tables, and remove both slot routing and exclusion subtraction.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A GeneralRecommender that uses K=4 fixed-count intent slots formed from attention over each user's train-history items, plus one exclusion prototype and candidate-conditioned routing, compared against an otherwise matched mean-history dot-product control.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does candidate-routed multi-intent user representation with an explicit exclusion channel outperform a matched single-vector collaborative filtering control?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: This should fit within the campaign budget because ML-1M histories are modest, K is small and fixed, and the main added cost is attention pooling over each user's train-history items plus routed full-sort scoring, which remains practical with cached history indices and batched computation.
